chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about whether the one in Ihram can scratch his head and wash with water. He (peace be upon him) said: He can scratch his head as long as he does not intend killing an insect, and there is no problem with him washing with water and pouring it over his head as long as he is not 'mulabbid' (covered with lice powder). If he is mulabbid, he should not pour water over his head except due to wet-dream.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.مُلَبِّداً: Covered with 'talbid' (a powder or substance used to kill lice)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for scratching and washing the head while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurarah, clarifies the permissibility of scratching the head and washing with water during Ihram, provided the primary intent is not to kill insects. It introduces a nuanced distinction regarding 'talbid' (a thick paste or powder used for lice), which restricts the direct pouring of water over the head unless necessitated by ritual impurity (janabah), reflecting the scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual purity with the preservation of the Ihram state.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the one in Ihraam, if he can scratch his head and wash (his head) with the water?’ Heasws said: ‘He can scratch his head for as long as he does not intend killing the insects; and there is no problem with him washing with the water, and he can pour upon his head for as long as he does not happen to have applied ‘talbid’ (lice powder). So, if he was such, having applied lice powder, so he should not pour the water upon his head, except if (after becoming impure) due to wet-dream’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram; if he can scratch his head and wash it with water. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can scratch his head as long as he is certain of not killing a moving thing but it is not harmful to wash with water unless one’s head is treated with talbid (a medicine against lice), in which case one must not pour water over his head except because of wet-dream.’”
